target_customer: Mobile app developers and mobile businesses needing customer support
problem: Web chat and helpdesk tools did not fit mobile apps, leaving app owners without good in-app support.
business_model: SaaS subscription priced 10 to 64 USD per month by integration level
product_category: In-app live chat and customer messaging

founders.name: Olufemi Omojola
founders.background_notes: Role from search coverage of a TechMoran interview; YC page lists no background

founders.name: Ayo Omojola
founders.background_notes: Named in TechCrunch January 2013; had built mobile products for about five years per TechMoran

competitors.name: Olark
competitors.what: Web live chat for support and sales

competitors.name: Zendesk
competitors.what: Helpdesk with chat based support on the web

technical_complexity.rationale: iOS and Android SDKs under 350 KB with real time chat and device context were real engineering for two people.

defensibility.rationale: SDK integration gave some lock in but Helpshift and larger helpdesks could add mobile chat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Conversocial acquired Hipmob in March 2017 and folded the brand into its platform.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in January 2013 said the mobile support market was underserved; customers included a taxi app in Mexico and several ecommerce firms.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found beyond product and acquisition news.

outcome_analysis: Hipmob built in-app chat for mobile developers out of the founders' own support struggles and was acquired by Conversocial in March 2017 in an all-stock deal for the technology. Funding appears limited to the YC deal, and no growth figures were published, so the outcome reads as a small technology acquisition.
notes: Website hipmob.com now redirects to a domain marketplace (dead). The 120K USD YC seed rests on a single database (Dealroom) and equals YC's standard deal, recorded as other. Third co-founder Gaurav Namit appears in search coverage of directory pages and is not recorded as a founder. Competitor source is a year after the batch. Founder education and employers not found. The YC directory marks the company Inactive because it was acquired; exit.type acquisition is correct and the conflict is only the directory label.
